title: Balance and Swap
topic: The equals sign and giving and taking

items.q: Fill in the missing number so both sides are the same: 5 + 3 = 4 + ___
items.hint: The 5 became 4. It went down by 1. So what happens to the 3?

slips.say: 8 is the total of 5 + 3. The blank is only one of the two numbers on the right side.

tpl.q: Fill in the missing number so both sides are the same: {a} + {b} = {c} + ___
tpl.hint: The {a} became {c}. It went down by {k}. So what happens to the {b}?

items.q: Fill in the missing number so both sides are the same: 4 + 7 = 6 + ___
items.hint: The 4 became 6. It went up by 2. So what happens to the 7?

slips.say: 11 is the total of 4 + 7. The blank is one of the numbers on the right side.

tpl.q: Fill in the missing number so both sides are the same: {a} + {b} = {c} + ___
tpl.hint: The {a} became {c}. It went up by {k}. So what happens to the {b}?

items.q: Which sum is the same amount as 6 + 4?
steps: The 6 went down by 1 and the 4 went up by 1.

slips.say: 5 + 4 makes 9. 6 + 4 makes 10. Add both sides first.

items.hint: 30 went up by 10 to 40. What happens to the other 30?
steps: So the other 30 goes down by 10.

slips.say: 60 is the total of 30 + 30. The blank is one of the two numbers on the right.

tpl.hint: {a} went up by 10 to {c}. What happens to the {b}?

items.q: Siti fills in 8 + 6 = 9 + ___. Which number goes in the blank?
items.hint: 8 + 6 makes 14. The right side must make 14 too. What goes with 9?
steps: The right side must make 14 too.
9 and 5 make 14, so the blank is 5.

slips.say: 14 is the total of the left side. The right side is 9 plus the blank, and that must also make 14.

items.hint: 49 went up by 1 to 50. What happens to the 26?

slips.say: 75 is the total. The blank is the number that goes with 50.
27 is 1 more than 26. The 49 went up, so 26 must go down.

tpl.hint: {a} went up by {y} to {c}. What happens to the {b}?

items.q: Do not add. Which sum has the same total as 47 + 18?
items.hint: 47 became a different number. Did the 18 move the opposite way by the same amount?

slips.say: Both numbers went down. One must go down and the other must go up.

items.q: Do not add. Which total is greater: 29 + 14 or 30 + 15?
items.hint: Did the numbers move the same way or opposite ways?
steps: Both went up, so 30 + 15 is greater.

slips.say: Both numbers went up by 1. That makes the total 2 greater.

items.q: Ben wrote 24 + 17 = 26 + 19. It is not balanced. What number should replace the 19?
items.hint: Look at how the first number moved. The other number must move the opposite way.
steps: So 17 must go down by 2, not up.

slips.say: 19 is what Ben wrote. Both numbers went up by 2, so the total is too big.

tpl.q: Ben wrote {a} + {b} = {c} + {d}. It is not balanced. What number should replace the {d}?
tpl.hint: {a} went up by {k} to {c}. The other number must move the opposite way.
steps: So {b} must go down by {k}, not up.

items.q: Fill in both blanks: 19 + 28 = 20 + ___ = ___ + 30. There are two blanks. Type both numbers in order, with a comma between them.
items.hint: Find the first blank by giving and taking. Then find the total, and the second blank.
steps: 19 went up by 1 to 20, so 28 goes down by 1 to 27.
47 take away 30 is 17. The blanks are 27 and 17.

items.q: Mei has 28 stickers on a page and 17 in her pocket. Ali has the same total as Mei. He has 30 on a page. How many are in his pocket?
items.hint: Compare Ali's page with Mei's page. Does his pocket have more or fewer?
steps: Ali's page has 2 more than Mei's.
So his pocket has 2 fewer than 17.

slips.say: 17 is Mei's pocket. Ali has more on his page, so fewer in his pocket.

tpl.q: Mei has {a} stickers on a page and {b} in her pocket. Ali has the same total as Mei. He has {c} on a page. How many are in his pocket?
tpl.hint: Compare Ali's page with Mei's page. Does his pocket have more or fewer?
steps: Ali's page has {k} more than Mei's.
So his pocket has {k} fewer than {b}.

items.q: ___ + 5 = 9 + ___. The first blank is how many more than the second blank?
items.hint: Try a small number for the second blank. What must the first blank be?
steps: Try the second blank as 1: the right side is 10.
The first blank must be 5, which is 4 more than 1.
The first blank is always 4 more.

slips.say: 9 is on the right side already. Try numbers in the blanks and see how far apart they are.

tpl.q: ___ + {p} = {q} + ___. The first blank is how many more than the second blank?
tpl.hint: Try a small number for the second blank. What must the first blank be?
steps: Try the second blank as 1: the right side is {q} + 1.
The first blank plus {p} must match it.
The first blank is always {ans} more.

items.q: Make up your own puzzle like 27 + 14 = 30 + ___. Check it by adding both sides.
items.hint: Pick a sum first. Change one number, then work out the blank.
steps: Pick two numbers to add, for example 27 and 14.
Change the first number, for example to 30. It went up by 3.
The blank is 3 less than 14: it is 11. Check: 27 + 14 = 41 and 30 + 11 = 41.
